newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end easier in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly lower on Tuesday in thin trade with market players stuck on the sidelines seeking to shrug off the lingering effects of a long holiday, dealers said.
"The market had a hangover from the holidays. Everybody is still in a holiday mood. It was a dull and sleepy market," a local rubber trader said.
"There was some buying of RSS3 rubber from local manufacturers getting their monthly requirement, but the overall volume in the market was thin," another trader said.
The rubber market was closed on Monday for a holiday.

Soft Japanese prices depressed sentiment in the local market, traders said. Tokyo's benchmark April contract fell 1.3 yen to settle at 140.9 yen while Kobe's April contract settled at 141.0 yen from the previous 142.0 yen.
At around 0945 GMT, December RSS3 was seen at 125.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg against Friday's settlement of 126.75 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 182.25-184.25 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.32) a kg from the previous 184.25 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 177.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26-$1.28) a kg against 179.00 cents.
